documents.title: Conference Call with the Fund Managers, Analysts and Investors - Transcript
Presentation - Conference Call with the Fund Managers, Analysts and Investors on October 29, 2026

analysis.summary: Wheels India Limited reported financial and operational results for Q2 and H1 FY27, noting growth in export revenues and overall sales. Management outlined a capex estimate for FY27 in the range of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs targeting expansion across multiple segments. Strategic focus areas include growing exports, ramping up cast aluminium and wind energy components, and optimizing working capital. Key financial metrics reflect improvements in gross revenues and profitability alongside ongoing debt and cash flow management. Wheels India Limited released its investor presentation for Q1 FY27, reporting standalone gross revenues of Rs 1,386.07 crs and a consolidated gross revenue of Rs 1,492.79 crs.

guidance.claim: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs.
guidance.quote: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs

capex_expansion.claim: Capex is towards expansion of capacity in auto steel wheels, cast alloy wheels, energy products division including large machining, hydraulic cylinders, construction & mining wheels and air suspension.
capex_expansion.quote: This capex is towards expansion of capacity in auto steel wheels, cast alloy wheels, energy products division including large machining, hydraulic cylinders, construction & mining wheels and air suspension .

capex_expansion.claim: Management stated plans to ramp-up the expanded facility for machining of large castings for windmills and step up capacity for fabricated parts.
capex_expansion.quote: Ramp-up the expanded facility for machining of large castings for windmills; Also Step up the capacity and volumes of the fabricated, structural parts for windmills, including off- shore WEGs

capex_expansion.claim: The company spent INR 261 crores towards capex in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: In terms of capex, last year, we basically spent about INR261 crores towards capex, which is both in terms of investment towards the windmill business, aluminium business and a little bit of the off-road businesses and some routine capex and cost savings totalling INR261 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Management expects capex in the current year to be between INR 280 crores and INR 300 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: And we expect in the current year, it will be between INR280 crores to INR300 crores of capex.

capex_expansion.claim: The board-approved capex for financial year 2026-27 is about INR 280 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: One is the capex approved for the Board is about INR280 crores at the moment.

capex_expansion.claim: The company's current aluminium wheel capacity is about 42,000 per month and is being increased to 60,000 and then to 80,000.
capex_expansion.quote: In aluminium wheels we currently have a capacity of about 42,000 per month. We are increasing it -- in a few months we are increasing it to 60,000 and then by half year, we'll increase it to 80,000.

margins_costs.claim: Cost optimization is a key strategy with a thrust on profitability.
margins_costs.quote: Cost optimization, with a thrust on profitability

margins_costs.claim: The company recorded a net forex profit of about INR 4 crores for the quarter and close to INR 10 crores for the whole year.
margins_costs.quote: So in the current quarter, we had a profit of about INR4 crores as a net thing on the forex. And for the whole year, it is about close to INR10 crores as forex gain.

margins_costs.claim: Management noted that inventory provisions were higher due to the adoption of a more stringent phased provisioning rule.
margins_costs.quote: And inventory provisions are higher because a company has adopted a more stringent rule for provisioning. As a consequence, the provision for inventory has been higher in this quarter as well as for the whole year.

orders_capacity.claim: Combined passenger car steel wheel capacity between Wheels India and its subsidiary is approximately 11 million to 12 million.
orders_capacity.quote: So if you take passenger car, steel wheels between us and our subsidiary, if I look at it combined, I think Wheels India has got a capacity of about 4 million and the subsidiary has got a capacity of about 7 million. So about 11 million to 12 million is the capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company has a capacity of 50,000 large wheels per month for the tractor industry.
orders_capacity.quote: take the tractor industry, if you count it in terms of the larger wheels as opposed to the smaller wheels, we have a capacity of 50,000 a month.

capital_allocation.claim: The company focuses on funding capex predominantly through accruals and holding the debt at current levels.
capital_allocation.quote: Fund capex predominantly thro accruals and holding the debt at current levels

capital_allocation.claim: Working capital optimization and cash flow management are highlighted as focus areas.
capital_allocation.quote: Working capital optimization and cash flow management

management_commitments.claim: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs.
management_commitments.quote: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs

management_commitments.claim: Management expects double-digit EBITDA within the next 1 or 2 years.
management_commitments.quote: I think as and when that happens, I think we're probably 2 years away -- 1 or 2 years away from double-digit EBITDA. I don't think it should take longer than that.

management_commitments.claim: Management targets an ROCE of 18% plus and a return on equity of 15% plus.
management_commitments.quote: I would look at our ROCE being 18% plus, I would look at our return on equity to be 15% plus.

management_commitments.claim: Management aims to increase the company's stake in Axles India to roughly 15% to 20% or 25% over a period of time.
management_commitments.quote: So the idea was that Wheels India can get improve its stake, so we are looking at maybe something like 15%, maybe slightly higher, 20%, 25% over a period of time.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
